items.n: L'Herboriste, le vol en mortier, fond crème
items.p:
Image 1 is a blank sheet of cream #F2E9D7 paper: paint the new illustration directly on it and keep its exact proportions. Images 2, 3 and 4 are the STYLE REFERENCES: copy exactly their technique and look: contemporary flat gouache illustration, smooth sculpted shapes, broad flowing fabric folds painted in clean bands of colour, soft brushed gouache texture, very fine discreet outlines, elegant stylized figure, the subject and the few scene elements named below on a plain ground. Never copy their subjects. No decorative extras: no ribbons, no bells, no stars, no flowers, no discs, no ornaments.

SUBJECT — "L'Herboriste": a single chimera, a herbalist with the head of a hare with long ears on a woman's body, wearing a long dress with an apron. She flies high through the air across the upper part of the sheet, sitting inside a huge stone mortar like the witch of the old tales, steering it with a giant pestle held like an oar and leaning hard into the turn. The mortar is clearly airborne, far above the bottom of the sheet, and a long trail of leafy herbs falls from it toward the ground below. Her ears stream backward in the wind; her face is calm, as if this were her ordinary way to commute. Scene elements: the mortar, the pestle and the falling herbs, nothing else. The scene is a fairy tale told with wit: lively, poetic, and slightly offbeat or absurd where the action calls for it, played deadpan, never cute. The scene elements are few and simple, painted in the same flat gouache bands as the figure.

PALETTE: only oxblood red #560002, dark olive #3B3302, sky blue #A6C8FF and cream #F2E9D7. The figure and the scene elements are painted in sky blue, oxblood red and olive on the cream #F2E9D7 background.

LAYOUT: the whole sheet is a plain cream #F2E9D7 ground with a subtle paper texture, no frame and no border. The figure is large and fills the sheet, its extremities close to the edges, but the whole figure stays entirely inside the sheet, nothing cropped. No text, no letters, no numbers, no signature.

ABSOLUTE RULE, FLOATING COMPOSITION: there is no ground, no floor, no ground line, no strip of earth or grass, no horizon, no water line and no frame. The figure and every element float freely on the plain dark olive background. The plain dark olive background surrounds every drawn element on all four sides: nothing touches or is cut by the edges of the sheet, and only the dark olive background colour reaches the four edges. If anything in image 1 touches or is cut by an edge of the sheet, or stands on a strip of ground, remove that ground and bring the element fully inside the sheet with a clear margin of dark olive background around it; you may scale the whole drawing down slightly to achieve this.

ADD a few small decorative elements that belong to this character's world and tell a little of its story, floating in the empty areas of the background around the figure: three or four loose pages flying out of the books and fluttering away, a quill pen drifting, a small inkwell, a thin crescent moon and four or five small eight-pointed stars. They are small in scale, naive and emblematic, painted flat in the same gouache technique as the figure with very fine discreet outlines, each one fully surrounded by dark olive background, never touching the figure nor the edges of the sheet. The figure stays the clear centre of the image.

items.n: La Conteuse licorne, debout sur la pile de livres, déclame, fond olive
items.p:
Image 1 is a finished flat gouache panel, "La Conteuse", on a plain dark olive background. Use image 1 as the reference for everything except the creature: the same flat gouache technique with very fine discreet outlines, the same brushwork and paper texture, the same four colours, the same dark olive background, the same proportions of the sheet, the same kind of small floating decorative elements (loose pages fluttering, a quill, a small inkwell, a crescent moon, small eight-pointed stars) and the same pile of books.

REPLACE THE CREATURE with a new chimera, the reverse of a centaur: the top half is a unicorn and the bottom half is a woman. From the waist up: a white unicorn with a horse's head, a long spiral horn, a flowing mane, a horse's neck and chest, and two front legs with hooves used like arms. From the waist down: a woman's hips and legs in a short flared skirt, wearing funny boots: long pointed boots with toes that curl up into a spiral, mismatched stripes, a small pompom or bell on each tip. The joke is played deadpan, elegant, never cute. The unicorn is the storyteller: mouth open, declaiming her tale with feeling.

POSE AND SCENE: She stands proudly on top of the floating pile of books, one boot forward, front hooves raised wide as she declaims to the sky, a small harp tucked under one hoof.

ABSOLUTE RULE, FLOATING COMPOSITION: no ground, no floor, no ground line, no horizon. The creature, the books and every element float freely on the plain dark olive background, which surrounds every drawn element on all four sides. Nothing touches or is cut by the edges of the sheet; only the dark olive background reaches the four edges.

Palette: only oxblood red #560002, dark olive #3B3302, sky blue #A6C8FF and cream #F2E9D7. The unicorn is cream with sky blue and oxblood accents in the mane; the skirt and boots in oxblood, sky blue and cream stripes. No other colours. No text, no letters, no musical notes, no signature.

items.p:
Image 1 is a gouache panel, "La Conteuse": a reverse centaur, unicorn on top and woman's legs below, standing with a floating pile of books on a dark olive background. Image 2 is a reference ONLY for how mature, noble and elegant the unicorn must look. Do not copy from image 2 its letters, its wings, its red background or its composition.

REDRAW THE CREATURE OF IMAGE 1 MORE MATURE, in the spirit of the unicorn of image 2: a noble, realistic and elegant horse anatomy, a long refined head with a fine muzzle, flared nostrils, a dark almond eye with a calm, grave expression, small pointed ears, a long thin spiral horn, a long arched neck. The mane and the tail are long flowing locks painted with dense visible gouache strokes, cream with sky blue shadows and touches of oxblood, as in image 2. The front legs are slender horse legs with fine dark hooves, used like arms with grace. The lower half stays a woman: long elegant legs, a refined flared skirt, and the curled-toe striped boots, now drawn with finesse and restraint rather than as a cartoon. Nothing cute, nothing childish: a poised, grown-up, slightly ironic figure. The unicorn still tells her tale, mouth slightly open.

Keep from image 1: the pose and gesture of the creature, the composition, the floating pile of books, the small floating decorative elements (pages, quill, inkwell, crescent moon, stars), the dark olive background and the proportions of the sheet. The paint handling becomes richer and more painterly, with visible brushwork like image 2, while staying clean and readable.

items.n: La Dame du Lac, le plongeon droit vers l'anneau, fond crème
items.p:
Image 1 is a blank sheet of cream #F2E9D7 paper: paint the new illustration directly on it and keep its exact proportions. Images 2, 3 and 4 are the STYLE REFERENCES: copy exactly their technique and look: contemporary flat gouache illustration, smooth sculpted shapes, broad flowing fabric folds painted in clean bands of colour, soft brushed gouache texture, very fine discreet outlines, elegant stylized figure. Never copy their subjects. No decorative extras beyond the scene elements listed below.

SUBJECT, "La Dame du Lac": a single chimera, the Lady of the Lake as a mermaid: a woman with long flowing hair painted in oxblood red and a small crown, in a fitted bodice with flowing sky blue sleeves, her lower body a long fish tail with large checkered scales in sky blue, oxblood and olive, ending in a wide flowing fin. She dives down to recover a ring lost at the bottom of the lake. She dives straight down head first, her body and tail forming one long vertical S-curve from the top of the sheet, both arms stretched down ahead of her, her hair streaming upward behind her like a flame. At the bottom of the sheet, a small round floating mound of lake floor with a gold ring resting on it; her fingertips are just above the ring. Scene elements: a gold ring with one small stone on a small floating mound of sand with two tufts of water plants, a trail of bubbles rising from her, two small fish swimming away, nothing else. The scene is a fairy tale told with wit: lively, poetic, played deadpan, never cute. The scene elements are few, small and simple, painted in the same flat gouache bands as the figure.

ANATOMY: one correct, graceful, well proportioned body: a natural human head, neck, shoulders and two arms of normal length, each hand with five fingers; the waist joins the fish tail smoothly at the hips; the tail is one continuous elegant curve, no twisting, no extra limbs, no distorted or stretched torso.

PALETTE: only oxblood red #560002, dark olive #3B3302, sky blue #A6C8FF and cream #F2E9D7. The ring is painted in cream and dark olive with a fine oxblood outline so it reads as gold. The figure and the scene elements are painted in sky blue, oxblood red and olive on the cream background.

LAYOUT, FLOATING COMPOSITION: the whole sheet is a plain cream ground with a subtle paper texture, no frame, no border, no ground line, no horizon, no water surface. The mermaid is large and fills most of the sheet, and every element floats on the cream background, which surrounds the whole drawing on all four sides with a clear margin: nothing touches or is cut by the edges of the sheet; only the cream background reaches the four edges. No text, no letters, no numbers, no signature.

items.n: Le Héraut flottant, bras corrigés A, fond bleu ciel
items.p:
Image 1 is a finished flat gouache illustration of "Le Héraut": a rooster-headed herald in a striped doublet blowing a long trumpet with a pennant, striding among unrolling scrolls, on a plain sky blue background with small floating decor (sun, clouds, feathers, bell, weathervane).

FIX ONLY THE ARMS. In image 1 both arms come out of the same shoulder on the right side of the torso, which is anatomically wrong. Redraw them so that there is exactly one arm on each side of the torso, each arm attached to its own shoulder and its own puffed striped sleeve:
- The arm on the right side of the image rises from the right shoulder and holds the trumpet to the beak, as in image 1.
- The arm on the left side of the image comes out of the large puffed sleeve on the left shoulder and holds the long scroll, the hand gripping the top of the scroll at chest height or slightly to the side, so the scroll still unrolls down and around his legs as in image 1.
Two arms, two hands with five fingers, natural proportions, no extra limb, no arm crossing behind the neck.

Keep everything else identical to image 1: the rooster head, the comb, the trumpet and its pennant, the striped doublet and its colours, the belt, the legs and pointed shoes, the stride, the scrolls, the sun, the clouds, the feathers, the bell, the weathervane, the brushwork, the paper texture, the sky blue background, the framing and the proportions of the sheet. Floating composition: nothing touches the edges of the sheet.

SUBJECT, "Le Héraut": a single chimera, a herald with the head of a rooster with a big comb on a man's body, in a striped tabard with puffed sleeves, a belt, hose and pointed shoes. items.n: La Conteuse pégase licorne, debout sur la pile de livres, déclame, fond olive
items.p:
Image 1 is a finished flat gouache panel, "La Conteuse", on a plain dark olive background. Use image 1 as the reference for everything except the creature: the same flat gouache technique with very fine discreet outlines, the same brushwork and paper texture, the same four colours, the same dark olive background, the same proportions of the sheet, the same kind of small floating decorative elements (loose pages fluttering, a quill, a small inkwell, a crescent moon, small eight-pointed stars) and the same pile of books.

REPLACE THE CREATURE with a new chimera, the reverse of a centaur: the top half is a winged unicorn, a Pegasus with a horn, and the bottom half is a pair of human legs. From the waist up: a noble white winged unicorn with a horse's head, a long spiral horn, a horse's neck and chest, two large feathered wings rising from the shoulders, and two front legs with hooves used like arms. The mane is SHORT: clipped close or tightly plaited along the neck like a dressage horse, never long and never loose. From the waist down: human legs in plain fitted riding breeches and BIG TALL RIDING BOOTS, heavy leather equestrian boots rising above the knee with wide cuffs and small spurs, sturdy and a little oversized, which is the deadpan joke. The waist is covered by the short tails of a fitted riding jacket that ends at the hips. NO skirt, no dress, no bare skin on the legs, no long flowing hair, no feminine curves emphasised, nothing sensual or suggestive.

TONE: mature, elegant and heraldic, like a figure from a medieval tapestry or a coat of arms, painted with dry wit. Never childish, never cute, no big round eyes, no pastel sweetness. The unicorn is the storyteller: mouth slightly open, declaiming her tale with gravity.

POSE AND SCENE: She stands upright on top of the floating pile of books, one riding boot planted forward, wings half open, both front hooves raised as she declaims to the sky.

ABSOLUTE RULE, FLOATING COMPOSITION: no ground, no floor, no ground line, no horizon. The creature, the books and every element float freely on the plain dark olive background, which surrounds every drawn element on all four sides. Nothing touches or is cut by the edges of the sheet; only the dark olive background reaches the four edges.

Palette: only oxblood red #560002, dark olive #3B3302, sky blue #A6C8FF and cream #F2E9D7. The unicorn and its wings are cream with sky blue shading; the riding jacket in oxblood; the breeches cream; the riding boots in oxblood or dark olive outlined in cream so they read clearly on the olive ground. No other colours. No text, no letters, no musical notes, no signature.

No skirt, no long hair, nothing sensual. Mature, elegant and heraldic tone with dry wit, never childish, never cute. Her eyes are OPEN and clearly visible, a calm almond-shaped horse eye with a dark pupil, never closed.

WINGS: two very large feathered wings, cream with sky blue, FULLY SPREAD and raised UPWARD above her shoulders in a wide heraldic V, their long flight feathers reaching up and out into the upper corners of the sheet so that the wings fill the empty space above and around her, like a crest on a coat of arms.

SCENE: she SITS on a LOW pile of only four or five books, no taller than her lower legs, floating in the lower part of the sheet. She holds a large OPEN BOOK in her two front hooves, pages spread wide, and reads it aloud, mouth slightly open. One big riding boot is crossed over the other knee, her eyes on the open book. A few small decorative elements float around her, small and simple: two or three loose pages, a quill, a crescent moon and a few small eight-pointed stars.

PALETTE: only oxblood red #560002, dark olive #3B3302, sky blue #A6C8FF and cream #F2E9D7. The pages of the open book are blank cream: no text, no letters, no signature.

ABSOLUTE RULE, FLOATING COMPOSITION: no ground, no floor, no ground line, no horizon, no frame. The creature, the books and every element float freely on the plain dark olive background. The figure with its wings is large and fills the sheet, but the dark olive background surrounds the whole drawing on all four sides with a clear margin: no wing tip, no boot and no book touches or is cut by the edges of the sheet; only the dark olive background reaches the four edges.

Top-down product mockup photograph of one single tall narrow vertical menu card, very elongated proportion of 10 by 21 centimetres, lying flat and centred on a pale warm grey linen tablecloth, soft even daylight, the whole card visible with margin around it. The card is thick uncoated deep burgundy cotton paper, colour sang-de-boeuf #560002. The only printing on the card is hot-foil stamping in two flat layers. Layer one, underneath: a fish, stamped in flat opaque matte white foil. Layer two, on top: a lamb, stamped in flat bright silver metallic foil, printed over the white fish and fully opaque where the two overlap, so the silver hides the white there. Each foil is one perfectly uniform solid area with crisp clean edges and a very slight debossed relief pressed into the paper. The drawing is made of bold, simple, flat shapes with thick strokes and a few large internal cut-outs, like a hand-carved linocut reduced to its essentials, readable from across a table. Plenty of empty burgundy paper around the figures. The card surface carries no lettering at all. Composition: a tight close-up crop. Only fragments are on the card: the white fish's large eye, gills and part of the head enter from the bottom edge, filling the lower half; the silver lamb's head and one ear enter from the top edge, looking down, overlapping the fish's head in the middle. Both animals bleed off the card edges.

Studio product photograph, top-down, of one single tall narrow vertical menu card, very elongated proportion of 10 by 21 centimetres, lying flat and centred on a pale warm grey linen tablecloth, soft even daylight, the whole card visible with margin around it. The card is thick uncoated deep burgundy cotton paper, colour sang-de-boeuf #560002. The only printing is hot-foil stamping in two flat layers: underneath, a salmon in flat opaque matte white foil; on top, a lamb in flat bright silver metallic foil, printed over the white and fully opaque where they overlap. Each foil is one perfectly uniform solid area with crisp edges and a slight debossed relief in the paper. Drawing language of contemporary independent illustration posters: bold flat silhouettes, a few confident cut lines inside the shapes that reveal the burgundy paper, each cut line at least as thick as a pencil stroke; wild, expressive, slightly menacing creatures with dynamic twisted bodies, sharp and adult, with dry humour. The card carries no lettering. Relationship and composition: heraldic mirror symmetry along the vertical axis: two salmon in white arch outward forming a lyre shape on the lower two thirds; a single silver lamb stands frontally between their curved bodies at the top, rearing, its legs hooked over the fish. Strong ornamental silhouette with bold internal cuts.

Image 1 is a reference for the card, the paper, the two hot-foil layers, the photography and the vigour of the poses; generate a new design on the same card. The card: one tall narrow vertical menu card, proportion 10 by 21 centimetres, thick uncoated deep burgundy cotton paper, colour #560002, photographed flat from above on a pale warm grey linen cloth, soft even daylight, the whole card visible. The printing is only hot-foil stamping in two flat layers: the salmon in matte white foil underneath, the lamb in bright silver foil on top, opaque where they overlap. Each foil is a uniform solid area with crisp edges and a slight debossed relief; inner details are thin burgundy cut lines in the foil, with no gradients and no shading. The card carries no lettering. Drawing style: a medieval illuminated bestiary drawing, as in thirteenth-century English bestiaries and manuscript marginalia, translated into flat foil. Elongated, stylised animal bodies; the lamb's fleece drawn as rows of small tight spiral curls; the salmon's scales as a regular pattern of small crescents; fins and tails drawn like ornamental leaves; a few slender medieval vine tendrils ending in trefoil leaves. Confident outlines, decorative and precise, while the bodies keep the strong twisting energy of Image 1. The drawing avoids any Japanese woodblock character: no wave motifs, no ukiyo-e brushwork. Faces are calm and neutral: mouths closed, no teeth, a simple almond-shaped medieval eye, a serene gaze. Composition, a variation on the logic of Image 1: the dancing lambs and salmon form a round, a tall oval ring of animals chasing each other head to tail around an empty centre, with a few small eight-pointed stars. Density: airy. The figures are smaller and grouped in the lower two thirds of the card; a large calm area of empty burgundy remains in the upper part. The dance has about five animals in total, lambs and salmon.

Flat two-colour production artwork for vectorisation, on a plain pure white background, in a tall narrow vertical frame. Subject: a fish and a lamb meeting in a kiss, stacked vertically and filling the height of the frame. In the upper half, a large fish like a salmon dives head down: its body curves in a big C, the wide forked tail fanning up at the top right, the back arching to the left with the dorsal fin, two pectoral fins, a row of small oval spots along the back, a curved gill line, and the head pointing down at the centre. In the lower half, a young lamb rears up on its hind legs, seen from the side, its head raised straight up so that the tip of its nose touches the fish's closed mouth; one front leg is lifted high to the right with the hoof up, the other bent against its chest, the body sloping down to the left, a short curly tail at the left, the hind legs bent and kicking at the bottom, the ears held back horizontally. Drawing style: bold cut-paper and linocut silhouettes, sharp and confident, with a few thick white cut lines inside the shapes for the fins, the spots, the gill, the scalloped fleece curls and the hooves. Strong, dynamic, elegant, like a contemporary woodcut. Colours: the fish is one single flat solid colour, pure blue #1F4FBF; the lamb is one single flat solid colour, pure green #1E9E5A; every inner line is white. No gradient, no texture, no shadow, no outline of another colour, no paper, no card, no frame: only white, blue and green. Both eyes are drawn like real animal eyes, as in a natural history engraving, never like a human or cartoon eye: no white highlight dot, no round iris ring, no eyelashes, no eyebrows. Faces calm and neutral, mouths closed, no teeth. The fish's eye is one small solid round dot, cut out in white, with no highlight; its mouth is a long natural closed line following the jaw from the tip of the snout, touching the lamb's nose. The lamb's eye is a real sheep's eye set on the side of the head: a narrow horizontal almond outline with a heavy upper eyelid and a horizontal slit pupil, looking up at the fish.
